states.gap: B's ticks are a heavy filled ✔. Each one is about 2× the stroke of the label text next to it and nearly as tall as a capital, so 'Web', 'Duo' and 'Statistics' are marked in black blots. states.gapTheirs: The row labels in A's View menu don't line up. 'Enable Focus Mode', 'Hide Bars' and 'All Commands…' start at x≈1746 display px, while every other row, ticked or not, starts at x≈1761. That's a 15 display px (~22 device px) step down one column. B sets every label at one column (x≈1683), with the ticks hanging in a gutter to the left.
states.verdict: A's menu looks like it was built one row at a time. Its most important row and its last two rows break out of the label column, and anyone who has lived in a real menu bar notices that ragged edge at once. B is longer, but it's one grid: labels, submenu chevrons, shortcuts and small-caps section headings all line up, and its stats bar reads as calmly as the prose. B's clumsy ticks are the lesser fault next to A's broken column.

states.name: stats-menu
states.gap: The menu shows a wrong state: 'Hide Statistics' has a check mark even though all three statistics are visible in the bar under it. That's a fourth tick on a command, not a setting, so reading the menu tells the writer the statistics are both shown and hidden. The ticks are also a heavy filled glyph, about 2× the stroke weight of the menu text, where A uses a hairline check.
states.gapTheirs: The Stats menu isn't anchored to the bar it opens from. The bar's counts are centred at about x=1000 (display px), but the menu's panel sits at x≈1420–1680. That puts its left edge about 420 display px (about 600 device px) right of the bar's centre, next to the Characters cell rather than over it. The bar also shows no pressed or hover state, so nothing on screen links the click to the menu that opened.
states.verdict: B's menu opens where you clicked: it sits on the bar, which lights up as a grey pill, so the counts and their settings read as one control. A throws the menu off to the right edge of the text column, and you look away from the numbers you just clicked to find their options. B then spoils this with a check next to 'Hide Statistics' while the statistics sit in plain view, which is the kind of state bug that makes a writer stop trusting every other tick. B still wins on placement, but not by much.

states.name: selection
states.gap: The pale-blue fill behind each held figure ('25', '124', '< 1 min') makes three separate chips in a 26 px bar. Together with the bar's wider spread (about 800–1200 px against A's 813–1187 px at display scale) and figures in near-body ink (#1D1D1D), the foot pulls the eye more than A's quiet grey row. On the page, B's selection fill spills beyond the text column: the first line's fill reaches about 1692 px, past the 1565 px measure, and the second line's starts about 125 px left of the text edge at 307 px. The selection looks like a ragged slab instead of a band that follows the text.
states.gapTheirs: The title shows the file extension, 'Untitled.md', which makes it about 110 px wide against B's bare Document name. The stats bar uses two greys: figures at roughly #444 and labels ('words', 'characters', 'read') at roughly #999. While a run is held, only the cyan 'Selection' label marks it. The figures carry no fill, so the counts look no different from the whole-Document counts at a glance.
states.verdict: Both windows use the same thin chrome: a Library toggle, a centred name, a View glyph and a one-line count that sits at the very bottom. B's foot says 'these numbers are your selection' by marking the figures themselves, so you don't have to read the small cyan word first. A's two-grey row is quieter, but the held counts are easy to mistake for the whole-Document totals, and the '.md' in the title is filesystem noise. B wins by a little, and its fill spilling into the margin is the one thing on the page a writer would notice.
